terminalResult: For bounded operator-valued Schur-Herglotz responses on separable Hilbert space, the positive operator-valued measure is the lossless real-axis object. Scalarized nontangential a.e. density, topology-labelled atoms, singular-continuous mass, principal values, threshold scaling, approach geometry and Schur inverse control remain separate decorations. Every technically actionable bounded boundary discriminant has a disposition.

findings.statement: The positive operator-valued representing measure is the lossless boundary object; a pointwise boundary operator is a derived, topology-qualified object.
Scalar matrix elements have nontangential boundary values almost everywhere, with imaginary part equal to pi times the absolutely continuous density.
A bounded POVM can have finite scalar densities but no bounded B(H)-valued pointwise density.
Sigma({lambda}) is recovered by y Im M(lambda+i y), with WOT/SOT/norm convergence separately licensed.
Strong atom recovery does not imply norm recovery when continuous spectral mass concentrates on nonuniformly narrowing coordinates.
A y^(-1/2) boundary divergence can have zero atom indicator; divergence is not synonymous with a pole.
Zero absolutely continuous density and zero atoms do not determine zero measure; singular-continuous mass survives.
Norm boundary limits commute with Schur elimination under invertibility of the limiting denominator.
Strong Schur limits require strong-* factor convergence and a uniform inverse bound.
WOT factor limits are not multiplicative; shift powers have weakly zero factors and identity products.
Strong-* convergence without uniform inverse control can produce unbounded moving Schur corrections.
Where the topology permits Schur gluing, W_eff=W_A+B D_0^(-*) W_D D_0^-1 B*.
An eliminated boundary zero can create a positive atom in the effective response.
A sparse-spike density has its expected vertical limit at a Lebesgue point but a different limit along tangential spike-centre paths.
The real principal value is nonlocal decoration and neither follows from the pointwise density value nor replaces the full measure.
A generic a.e. Herglotz boundary theorem is not a uniform limiting-absorption principle; the latter needs a model and weighted/operator scale.

externalFrontiers.reentryCondition: Declare closed operators, common form domains, graph topology and domain transport under adjoints and Schur elimination.
Choose a Hamiltonian/PDE, threshold set and weighted or Besov operator scale, then prove a uniform resolvent estimate.
Include boundary values of off-diagonal blocks and a replacement passivity identity.
Specify the nonlinear response object, causality notion and replacement for linear positive operator measures.

boundedBoundaryExhaustion.scope: bounded operator-valued Schur-Herglotz responses on separable Hilbert space, real-axis nontangential boundary values, scalarization and topology-labelled operator upgrades
boundedBoundaryExhaustion.qualification: Exhaustion is relative to bounded operator-valued Herglotz responses on separable Hilbert space and topology-labelled real-axis boundary gluing; it does not cover unbounded domains or model-specific uniform LAP estimates.
